title: Importance of Recitation of the Quran
summary: Reciting the Quran grants immense spiritual benefits, including intercession and heart purification.
translation:
It should be part of our routine that recitation of the Holy Quran is an important part of our lives and routines. Through recitation of the Quran lies life for us personally and great provisions for the Hereafter, as it will intercede for us in front of Allah Almighty, testifying that this person recited the Quran. This is why Allah had the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) speak of such virtues of the Quran, indicating the value of a person and their status in the sight of Allah.

There is a Hadith: "Those who do not receive what they ask in supplication are given when they recite the Quran." Thus, if one is more dedicated to Quran recitation throughout the day than supplicating, it is said that the rewards they obtain surpass those of the supplicant. Therefore, as it is the Word of Allah, it expresses His greatness and contains His commandments, and through recitation, one's heart is cleansed of rust, much like how water rusts iron, rendering it useless. Likewise, a rusted heart cannot absorb fear and humility of Allah and becomes insignificant in His sight. As cleaning iron restores it to usefulness, similarly, a cleansed heart becomes capable of bowing in submission to Allah.

The cleansing of the heart involves two things: remembrance of death and frequent recitation of the Quran. There is significant reward from Allah for frequently reciting the Quran, even for those who stutter, as they receive double the reward: one for the effort and one for the recitation itself. Hence, no expert should consider that someone who stutters receives less reward, nor should a stutterer feel inadequate next to proficient reciters. Even if they stammer, just like experts are rewarded, they too are given double reward for their recitation and effort.

Make Quran recitation a routine in life. Before dawn, finish a portion of the Quran, and before sleep, complete another portion. It is best to complete one 'Manzil' daily, or if not possible, three parts, or at least one part should be recited. If that is not feasible, even one page is better than none. Reciting the Quran while looking at it enlightens our eyes, revives our hearts, and renews our promise to follow Shariah commands. May Allah grant us the ability to perform righteous deeds and bless us with a bond with the Holy Quran.
